scope: Shared anatomical bristle coordinates for pigment and film
Finger channels, forearm grooves and sole bands
checkpoints.testChange: Anatomical pigment tracks deliberately change floor coverage by 4.5% in the matched fixture. Floor liquid remains within its original 3% gate; pigment alpha and painted area must remain within 10%.

resolvedIssues.cause: Naga required a return after the atomic retry loop; the function now exits the loop before returning. Both final browser suites use the corrected build.

scope: Four cumulative checkpoints retain the accepted V22 brush and drainage response. V23 pressure redistribution and edge spray, V24 cohesion and finite transfer, V25 anatomical brush character and directional impacts, V26 wet/dry shading.

No alpha pool stamps were introduced. Pressure moves existing finite film; spray debits coating only after successful particle allocation. Caught carried-volume droplets accumulate atomic credits and become coating on the next contact update.

Drip cohesion reads snapshot mass. Drying history is sampled in accelerateFilm before spreadFilm writes residue; shared-edge flux stays symmetric. This remains an art-directed thin-film approximation, not calibrated blood rheology.
The 54 bristles, seven film banks, 900 particles, original paint resolution, GPU simulation and normal-play no-body/no-pigment-readback policy are retained.

V25 intentionally changes floor pigment shape. The old 3% alpha identity gate is now a 10% alpha/area retention gate; floor liquid still has its original 3% tolerance. See the V25 checkpoint for the measured change.

Isolated field/body uploads test individual transfers; real articulated grab paths test integration. Videos retain the actual dummy for fifteen seconds after release. Native performance is measured separately from recording.
MP4s use the same input path on each build. GPU ragdoll trajectories can diverge; the footage is a gameplay comparison, not a frame-identical physics replay.
